review.summary: Post-publication remote-delivery governance is sound and all four 0.2.4 delivery receipts verify. Attempt-3's blocking defect is genuinely fixed: the portable report now emits `phase`/`source_unchanged`, and a new regression executes the exact workflow heredoc against a real produced report with per-key negative cases. The retained CI-observer archive is now SHA-256 pinned in fingerprinted code, phase metadata and the governance report; AGENTS.md's mirror clause is synchronized through a byte-exact bounded exception; the two-suite gate exclusion is documented. Published payload immutability is proven by Git blob-OID/mode reconstruction against 6f18529, with no packaged file in the governance allowlist. Residual issues are documentation-only: the docs/CI.md Jobs table still describes the pre-governance CI route, and the chunk narrative omits the attempt-3 rejection. No blocker or high findings; the readiness chunk's own exhausted budget still blocks phase completion.

findings.description: The Jobs table still states that contracts-and-package "runs tools/check_phase.py --phase 28 --verification-only --contracts-only" with "83 credential-free commands" producing "phase-28-contracts.json". In this reviewed tree the workflow runs the governance route (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73), which check_phase.py:899-909 delegates entirely to postdelivery.qualify_portable: 7 governance suites plus retained-report/payload/registry verification writing phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json. No contracts, model, native-ledger, dependency-policy or privacy command executes on that route. test_ci.py:241 and :292 deliberately tolerate the optional flag, so no regression catches the mismatch, and docs/CI.md:168-179 contradicts the table.
findings.required_fix: Update the docs/CI.md Jobs row to describe the actual governance route (7 suites, retained host-report verification, public archive re-download, phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json) and keep the 83-command/phase-28-contracts.json description in the clearly historical section at docs/CI.md:181-184; extend test_ci.py to assert the Jobs row matches the workflow's selected route.

findings.description: The chunk review history records attempt 1 (36/50, rejected) and attempt 2 (43/50, accepted) but omits attempt 3's rejection at 41/50 and its CI-step defect, while docs/phase-status.json:9103 still presents "accepted_chunk_review": "docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-remote-delivery-attempt-02.json" without noting that acceptance was superseded by the attempt-3 rejection against the newer governance source. The rejection is recorded only in review_findings_disposition.remote_delivery_attempt_3 (docs/phase-status.json:9070-9080).
findings.required_fix: Add the attempt-3 rejection, its principal finding and disposition to docs/post-publication-governance.md, and mark post_publication_governance.accepted_chunk_review as stale/superseded (or point it at the current attempt) so no summary field implies the chunk is currently accepted.

findings.description: This scope-correction record asserts originalReviewSha256, originalChecksSha256 and the qualification boundary for the rejected readiness attempt, but nothing executes against it: it lives in docs/checks/ (excluded by postdelivery.excluded at tools/postdelivery.py:60-61 and review_phase.EXCLUDED_DIRECTORIES at tools/review_phase.py:15), is absent from the governance report's immutableEvidence (docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-remote-delivery-attempt-04.checks.json:8-41), and is referenced only as prose in docs/phase-status.json:9087 and docs/post-publication-governance.md:80. Unlike every other delivery receipt in this chunk, its claimed hashes are unverified by any gate.
findings.required_fix: Verify this record in tools/postdelivery.py (e.g. re-hash the referenced attempt-5 review/checks against its recorded digests and include the disposition file in immutableEvidence), with a negative regression in tools/test_postdelivery.py for a tampered digest or decision.

evidence: docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-remote-delivery-attempt-04.checks.json:75-203 records 8 commands, every exit_code 0, scope post_publication_governance, source_sha256 536dad68… matching the reviewed source and source_unchanged true; recorded unittest tails total 22+6+14+52+12+18+39 = 163, matching docs/phase-status.json:9104-9105 (qualification_commands 8, focused_tests 163).

Attempt-3 high finding resolved: tools/postdelivery.py:390 and :409 now emit "phase": 28 and "source_unchanged": True, and docs/checks/phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json:2-5 contains phase/source_unchanged/passed/source_sha256. tools/test_ci.py:46-141 runs the actual heredoc extracted from .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:74-82 against the report produced by the real qualify_portable call, asserts the exact two logged JSON lines, then deletes each of phase/source_sha256/source_unchanged/passed/checks and requires a KeyError naming the removed key.

Attempt-3 medium finding resolved: tools/postdelivery.py:27-38 pins the three retained CI-observer archive files by SHA-256; verify_historical_producers runs for both roots (tools/postdelivery.py:239-240) and in the portable route (:346); verify_producer_metadata (:124-129) requires docs/phase-status.json:9011-9016 to carry the identical current observerSha256 a1c1383c… and historicalArchiveSha256 map; the three paths appear in immutableEvidence (checks file lines 38-40); tools/test_postdelivery.py:147-156 mutates each archived file and requires rejection.

Attempt-3 low findings resolved: AGENTS.md:13 now names both the canonical Forgejo destination and the maintainer-authorized GitHub mirror plus the fourth delivery receipt, admitted only through the byte-exact clause substitution in tools/postdelivery.py:86-91 and proven narrow by tools/test_postdelivery.py:123-145 (appending unrelated policy text raises "authorized mirror clause"). docs/CI.md:175-179 documents the deliberate test_postdelivery/test_final_delivery_review exclusion and requires both suites in the next source-changing phase.

Four delivery receipts verify: docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.4.json:12-14 (archiveSha256 533294fe…, 1043927 bytes, sourceCommit 6f18529a…, yanked false, owner cdot65, releaseReadiness at :749-753); docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.4-observation-04.json and docs/checks/release-tag-github-v0.2.4-observation-04.json both record tagObject 2f7ad298… peeled to 6f18529a… on their respective remotes with governanceSourceSha256 536dad68…; docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-31-observation-04.json:2667-2671 records expectedJobCount 49, counts {success: 49}, contextsMatchConfiguredMatrix true.

CI observation integrity: observation-04 retains earlier pending rows for the same contexts (lines 1163-1169) so the max(created_at,id) tie-breaker in scripts/observe-release.py:92-109 is actually exercised; snapshot/runHistory digests at lines 1143/1158 equal the confirmation block at 2299/2314 within a 2.2 s window (1159-1161); runHistory preserves run 30 failure and run 31 success on 56a88d25… (1144-1157), enforced by tools/postdelivery.py:181-202 against docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-30-failure.json with counts {success:48, failure:1}.

Published payload immutability: tools/postdelivery.py:68-114 reconstructs Git blob OIDs and file modes for every tracked/untracked non-evidence path against RELEASE 6f18529a…, rejecting any symmetric difference outside GOVERNANCE_PATHS (:17-23). No GOVERNANCE_PATHS entry is packaged — crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:11 includes only src/**, examples/**, LICENSE, NOTICE, README.md — so "published_payload_unchanged" is substantiated; tools/test_postdelivery.py:96-121 proves rejection of non-allowlisted new files, deletion and symlink replacement.

Guard composition is executed, not asserted: the recorded canonicalGuard (checks file lines 53-73) shows /usr/bin/python3 tools/release_delivery.py --phase 28 --version 0.2.4 run in /home/cdot/development/cdot65/scm-sdk-rs-ts035 with exit 0, jobs 49, sourceCommit 6f18529a…, ciCommit 56a88d25…; tools/postdelivery.py:166-178 binds docs/checks/phase-28-composed-delivery-F.json to that actual execution across command, cwd, exit code, parsed result and stdout/stderr digests, with seven tampering cases in tools/test_postdelivery.py:475-497.

Observer security: scripts/observe-release.py is read-only (ls-remote plus GET), reads the token from the environment and never writes it to a receipt, disables redirects (:27-29), bounds responses to 8 MiB and pagination to 20 pages (:205-207, :212-220, :227-235), writes receipts with open('x') so prior observations cannot be overwritten (:278), and exits with a sanitized message on any failure (:316-319). The portable registry re-download in tools/postdelivery.py:379-387 is credential-free, no-redirect, 32 MiB-bounded and byte/length compared.

Budget governance is explicit and not inferred: docs/reviews/recovery-authorizations/2026-10-22.json grants only a phase-level final-delivery budget (questionCallId call_1601a73a…, maxFreshReviews 5), validated with a pinned digest over all 20 original readiness artifacts in tools/review_phase.py:62-94; tools/review_phase.py:121 bars the fifth-attempt exception whenever a review_budget is used; docs/phase-status.json:9107-9116 keeps the readiness-chunk recovery as an unanswered request, and docs/post-publication-governance.md:73-94 states that the attempt-5 rejection (39/50) cannot establish acceptance.
limitations: Read-only review: no commands, tests or network calls were executed. Check outcomes were read from the recorded stdout/stderr in docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-remote-delivery-attempt-04.checks.json; I could not recompute any SHA-256, so recorded digests are accepted as verified by the executed tools at source 536dad68….

The retained qualified checkout /home/cdot/development/cdot65/scm-sdk-rs-ts035 is outside this repository and was not inspected. The 105-command report, both compiler package proofs, the retained registry/package archives and the canonical guard execution are accepted as recorded by the composed guard rather than independently re-derived.

Remote state (Forgejo refs and CI, GitHub mirror refs, crates.io bytes) was not contacted. Tag, CI and registry claims rest on point-in-time receipts, which the design itself documents as non-atomic observations.

The governance variant of .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml has never run on a remote runner: run 31's 49 successful contexts belong to the published workflow at 56a88d25…, and docs/checks/phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json is a host-produced receipt. The governance route's correctness rests on static review plus the tools/test_ci.py:46-141 boundary regression.

Git history, diffs and the published bytes of ci.yml/AGENTS.md could not be read directly; the conclusion that only the allowed substitutions were applied follows from the successful immutable_inventory execution recorded in the composed-guard run.

Chunk-scope judgement only. The release-readiness chunk's latest review (docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-05.json, 39/50, rejected) with its exhausted budget and unanswered recovery request still blocks phase-28 completion; that is outside this chunk and was not re-adjudicated.
